newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cautiously welcomes Iraqi pledge.
newsitem.headline: France cautiously welcomes Iraqi pledge.

text.p: France on Friday cautiously welcomed an Iraqi statement that Iraq would stop firing at allied warplanes saying such a decision would help defuse tensions in the Gulf region.

The French Foreign Ministry said in a statement that it had been told by Iraqi authorities of their decision "to suspend military actions against allied surveillance planes patrolling northern and southern Iraq".
"France notes this decision with satisfaction. If confirmed, it would...contribute to defusing tension," the statement said.

Iraq said earlier it would stop attacks on U.S. and allied warplanes flying over its north and south as of midnight local time (2000 GMT), the Iraqi News Agency (INA) said, quoting an official spokesman for the ruling Revolutionary Command Council.
France had previously urged Iraq to refrain from shooting at allied aircraft patrolling the skies over Iraqi Kurdistan, saying such action was unacceptable.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said his statement did not constitute a warning, and praised Iraq for what he called positive talks with local leaders in Kurdish areas captured by guerrillas backed by Baghdad.
He also pledged special friendship for Kuwait in what seemed an increasingly acrobatic balancing act by Paris to stay on good terms with all sides as the Gulf tensions seemed to heighten.

"As long as Operation Provide Comfort (over northern Iraq) is under way, we call on the Iraqi authorities to avoid any action which could endanger the security of the pilots. As we have told Baghdad, any attack against a reconnaissance aircraft would be unacceptable," Rummelhardt said.

Describing the situation on the ground in Kurdistan as stabilised, he said: "The opening of a dialogue between Kurdish leaders and Baghdad is an important step on the road towards normalisation in the north."
The official also praised what he said were new statements by Iraq saying it was not threatening neighbouring Kuwait.
Kuwait has tightened its security after Bahgdad said on Thursday it would be committing an act of war if it allowed U.S. Stealth planes to use its territory for attacks against Iraq.
Rummelhardt said Paris was attached to the sovereignty of both countries and particularly to its friendship with Kuwait.
France was part of the Gulf War coalition that drove Iraqi invasion forces out of Kuwait in 1991.
It has since helped patrol the two no-fly zones over Iraq while simultaneously launching diplomatic efforts to break Iraq's isolation and reopen potential large markets to French goods.

President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday that France, which criticised last week's U.S. cruise missile strikes against Iraq, was committed both to Iraq's territorial integrity and to arrangements made by Western allies after the 1991 Gulf War.
